record.paper_title: On two long standing open problems on Lp-spaces
record.original_question: For each real p with 1 < p < infinity and p not equal to 2, does the Banach space Lp contain continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces? Here Lp denotes the usual Lebesgue space, a complemented subspace means the range of a bounded projection on Lp, and two Banach spaces are considered the same only when they are linearly isomorphic.

evidence.quote: J. Bourgain, H.P. Rosenthal and G. Schechtman constructed uncountably many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of Lp for 1 < p < infinity, p 6= 2 in [8] (it is unknown, whether there exists continuum such subspaces).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1 < p < \infty$ with $p \neq 2$, and let $L_p = L_p([0,1], \mathrm{Lebesgue})$ denote the usual real Lebesgue Banach space. A closed subspace $X \subseteq L_p$ is called complemented if there exists a bounded linear projection $P : L_p \to L_p$ with range $X$. Two Banach spaces are identified only when they are linearly (topologically) isomorphic. 

Question: Does $L_p$ contain a family of $2^{\aleph_0}$ (continuum many) pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces?
artifact.status_search_result: Bourgain, Rosenthal and Schechtman (1981) constructed uncountably many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of $L_p$ for $1<p<\infty$, $p\neq 2$, indexed by countable ordinals. Whether there are continuum many such subspaces appears to remain open; surveys and recent works (including 2025 work on Bourgain–Rosenthal–Schechtman spaces) still treat the cardinality question as unresolved, even though related problems on closed ideals of $\mathcal{L}(L_p)$ have seen recent progress (Johnson–Schechtman, 2021).

status_evidence.title: A Survey on the Complemented Subspace Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Bourgain, Rosenthal and Schechtman constructed uncountably many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of Lp indexed by countable ordinals.
status_evidence.claim: Only uncountably many (not known to be continuum many) complemented subspaces of Lp have been constructed.

status_evidence.title: Coordinate systems and distributional embeddings in Bourgain-Rosenthal-Schechtman spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent framework for the BRS spaces; cardinality question regarding continuum many non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of Lp not resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to study BRS spaces without settling the continuum-many question.
